Rajkumari Sayyam vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 3 January, 2024 Author: Gurpal Singh Ahluwalia Bench: Gurpal Singh Ahluwalia 1 Wp No.27010/2023 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh At Jabalpur Before Hon'Ble Shri Justice Gurpal Singh Ahluwalia On The 3rd Of January, 2024 Writ Petition No. 27010 of 2023 Between:- Smt. Rajkumari Sayyam W/O Shri Chaitram Sayyam, Aged About 45 Years, Occupation: Sarpanch Ganeshganj Janpad Panchayat Ganeshganj Janpad Panchayat Lakhnadon District Seoni (Madhya Pradesh) .....Petitioner (By Shri Umashankar Tiwari - Advocate) And The State Of Madhya Pradesh Through Principal Secretary Panchayat And Rural Development Department Vallabh Bhawan, Bhopal (Madhya Pradesh) .....Respondents
texts.facts: 2. It is the case of petitioner that she is an illiterate tribal woman, who was elected as Sarpanch of Gram Panchayat Ganeshganj, Janpad Panchayat Lakhanodon, District Seoni. For betterment of villagers, petitioner called a Gram Sabha for passing some resolution regarding improvement in village. Resultantly, a Gram Sabha was convened and resolutions dated 16.08.2022 and 12.09.2022 were passed. Gram Sabha by passing the resolution had earmarked the land for different projects and works. However, by order dated 24.01.2023 S.D.O. Lakhnadon, District Seoni directed for construction of certain buildings at the place which were earmarked for Government Primary School, Ganeshganj/Community Centre. The representation was also filed by petitioner on 30.01.2023 before Collector. However, no action was taken by him. Accordingly, S.D.O. Lakhnadon without permission of Gram Sabha forcefully collected construction material on the spot and also started digging pits with the help of PHE Department. Accordingly, petitioner filed W.P. No.3763/2023 before this Court which was disposed of by giving liberty to approach the Additional Commissioner by filing an appeal. Thereafter, petitioner filed an appeal under Section 3 of Madhya Pradesh Panchayat Raj Appeal and Revision Rules, 1995 before the Commissioner. However, Commissioner by order dated 26.04.2023 upheld the order passed by S.D.O. Lakhnadon and accordingly, without consent of Gram Sabha respondent started raising construction of high level water tank on the land where the community hall was to be constructed. Thereafter, another writ petition was filed by petitioner which was registered as W.P. No.10470/2023 and by order dated 04.05.2023 the parties were directed to maintain status quo. In view of the aforesaid situation, S.D.O. Lakhnadon issued a letter dated 10.05.2023 alleging that certain complaints of irregularities have been received against Sarpanch and Secretary, therefore, they should be investigated closely and accordingly, directed for production of documents of Gram Panchayat. Thereafter, a show cause notice dated 13.06.2023 was issued by C.E.O., Jila Panchayat Seoni which was duly replied by petitioner and denied all the charges and submitted relevant documents to demonstrate that no irregularities/misconduct was committed by her. 3. It is the claim of petitioner that she is an illiterate tribal woman, therefore, the entire auction procedure was conducted by Secretary, who had informed that Gram Sabha has got Rs.82,000/- more than the previous auction, which was accepted by petitioner, therefore, there was no fault on the part of petitioner. With regard to summoning of Gram Panchayat meeting, it was summoned by Secretary and therefore, only Secretary has knowledge about the meeting as per the rules. So far as meetings dated 25.07.2022, 03.08.2022, 12.09.2022, 07.11.2022, 13.11.2022, 09.01.2023, 02.04.2023, 03.04.2023, 16.06.2023, 21.06.2023 and 15.07.2023 were concerned, it is the case of petitioner that those meetings were organized by Secretary and so far as the meetings of the month of February and March, 2023 were concerned, the entire record was presented before the S.D.O. Lakhnadon. Thereafter, C.E.O. Jila Panchayat Seoni by order dated 12.09.2023 removed the petitioner from her post under Section 40(1) of Madhya Pradesh Panchayat Raj Avam Gram Swaraj Adhiniyam. Petitioner preferred an appeal before the Commissioner. However, the appeal has also been dismissed. Smt. Rajkumari Sayyam vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 3 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51999321/ 2 4. Challenging the order passed by C.E.O. Jila Panchayat Seoni as well as Commissioner, Jabalpur Division, Jabalpur, it is submitted by counsel for petitioner that no inquiry was conducted and petitioner has been removed only by issuing a show cause notice. This procedure adopted by respondent is contrary to law laid down by this Court in the cases of Vikram Singh v. State of M.P. and others reported in 2019 (1) JLJ 473, Ballabh Das Satal v. State of M.P. and others reported in 1998 (2) JLJ 303, Kailash Kumar Parmanad Dangi v. State of M.P. and others reported in 1999 (2) MPLJ 722. 5. Per contra, the petition is vehemently opposed by counsel for respondent. Respondent in its return has stated that petitioner has alleged mala fides against the officials. The allegations against the petitioner were that petitioner as well as Panchayat officials have auctioned the market place without following the due procedure. S.D.O. (Revenue) issued a show cause notice to the petitioner and Secretary of Gram Panchayat Ganeshganj which has been filed as Annexure P/8. Since the matter relates to Gram Panchayat, therefore, S.D.O. (Revenue) Lakhnadon, District Seoni instructed the Chief Executive Officer, Janpad Panchayat Lakhnadon, District Seoni to conduct an inquiry and inquiry was conducted by Chief Executive Officer, Janpad Panchayat Lakhnadon, District Seoni and petitioner was also called in the said inquiry. The notice given to petitioner and acknowledgment of receipt of the same has been placed on record as Annexure R/1. Petitioner did not appear before the inquiry committee but the Secretary appeared and in his presence the inquiry was conducted and an inquiry report dated 26.05.2023 was submitted. It is submitted that opportunity was given to petitioner while internal fact finding inquiry was being conducted and therefore, it is incorrect to say that no opportunity of hearing was given to petitioner. 6. 8. On 13.06.2023 a show cause notice was issued by Chief Executive Officer, Jila Panchayat Seoni. On 21.08.2023 the reply was submitted. On 12.09.2023 petitioner was removed from the post of Sarpanch, Gram Panchayat Ganeshganj by the order of C.E.O.-cum- Prescribed Authority, Jila Panchayat Seoni. On 11.10.2023 the appeal filed by petitioner was dismissed by Commissioner, Jabalpur Division, Jabalpur.

Sharma, (1996) 3 SCC 364 : AIR 1996 SC 1669 the Supreme Court after exhaustive survey of the earlier precedents has formulated the test of prejudice, that is, whether the person has received a fair hearing considering all things. That rule is as under:-- "(5) Where the enquiry is not governed by any rules/regulations/statutory provisions and the only obligation is to observe the principle of natural justice -- or, for that matter, wherever such principles are held to be implied by the very nature and impact of the order/action -- the Court or the Tribunal should make a distinction between a total violation of natural justice (rule of audi alteram partem) and violation of a facet of the said rule. In such cases, normally liberty will be reserved for the Authority to take proceedings afresh according to law, i.e., in accordance with the said rule (audi alteram partem), (b) But in the latter case, the effect of violation (of a facet of the rule of audi alteram partem) has to be examined from the stand-point of prejudice; in other words, what the Court or Tribunal has to see is whether in the totality of the circumstances, the delinquent officer/employee did or did not have a fair hearing and the orders to be made shall depend upon the answer to the said query". This was denial of fair hearing resulting in serious prejudice to the petitioner. In Ballabhdas v. State of M.P.1998 (2) JLJ 303, it has been observed by this Court that a full fledged enquiry is provided under section 40 of the Act. It contemplates 'due enquiry'. State of M.P, [1999 (2) MPLJ 722 : 1999 (2) JLJ 280], esteemed brother S.P Khare, J. considered the question and held that removal of Sarpanch under section 40 is a serious matter when he is removed and further disqualified for six years to be elected under the Act. It is not sufficient to give a mere lip-service to the requirement of law. It is not the subjective choice of the prescribed authority to get an inquiry held of any kind. It does not envisage a secret enquiry or a preliminary enquiry alone. That is made only for collection of evidence and at that stage there is no participation of the person against whom the action is sought to be taken. The words "as it may deem fit" have to be construed objectively and would mean an inquiry depending upon the facts and circumstances of each case. Some of the facts of the inquiry may be excluded if the facts are not very much in dispute or there are other circumstances to dispense with them. "You must hear the person who is going to suffer".
